cause: The Spark intake (CommonValidator._validate_spark_column) carried no pool type rule: 0479659, the fix of spark-mixed-type-pool-refused, lifted the one-type rule off Spark entirely instead of narrowing it (the pools failed on 0.8.1 too), so distincts and distincts_prop pools Spark cannot write unchanged validated, then failed at get_df (CANNOT_MERGE_TYPE, CANNOT_INFER_TYPE) or were written as Java object strings or nulls.
context: Standing operator confirmation (every found bug: register and fix, never ask); found by the main thread from the 0.8.2 rc-2 as-is review, widened by dd-code-reviewer (verdict 2026-11-01T210231Z); reproduced at feature/0.8.2 9c1351e and tag 0.8.1 with Spark 3.5.8 local. Severity HIGH: a validated spec fails at generation or writes corrupt values (block-list item 5). Contract: constitution invariant 3 and SPEC 0.8.2 rc-1 §5 (a spec 0.8.1 accepted is refused only when it failed or lost data on 0.8.1); the mixed pools Spark writes faithfully ([1, 2.5], ['x', None], [1, 'x'], [True, 'x']) stay accepted per the spark-mixed-type-pool-refused resolution.
expected: Constitution invariant 3: a spec that validates generates. The Spark intake refuses at construction, with a SpecValidationError naming the column, every distincts or distincts_prop pool whose values Spark cannot write unchanged into one column; every pool Spark writes faithfully stays accepted.
repro: python -c "import datetime as dt; from pyspark.sql import SparkSession, functions as F; from rand_engine.main.spark_generator import SparkGenerator; s=SparkSession.builder.master('local[1]').getOrCreate(); print(SparkGenerator(s, F, {'c': {'method': 'distincts', 'kwargs': {'distincts': [dt.date(2020, 1, 1), 'x']}}}).size(20).get_df().collect()); SparkGenerator(s, F, {'c': {'method': 'distincts', 'kwargs': {'distincts': [1, True]}}}).size(5).get_df().collect()"
solution: method_specs._spark_pool_problem asks the engines instead of modelling them: on the pool Spark merges (distincts as given; distincts_prop's positive-weight keys in order), it builds the column as SparkCore.gen_distincts does with pandas, accepts the typed dtypes Spark writes, and folds an object or string column's values through pyspark's own _infer_schema/_merge_type and toInternal; it refuses merge or conversion failures, date/timestamp/binary beside text, container values, an all-null non-float column, and integers outside int64 (a690336).
symptom: SparkGenerator(spark, F, spec) constructs without error, then: a pool mixing bool with a number ([1, True], [1.5, False]), a date or datetime with a number ([date(2020,1,1), 1]) or a date with a datetime raises PySparkTypeError CANNOT_MERGE_TYPE at get_df; a pool mixing a date or datetime with text ([date(2020,1,1), 'x']) generates a string column whose date rows read 'java.util.GregorianCalendar[...]'. distincts and distincts_prop ({1.5: 1, False: 1}, {date: 1, 2: 1}, {date: 1, 'x': 1}) behave alike.
title: SparkGenerator accepts distincts and distincts_prop pools whose mixed types Spark cannot hold, then fails at get_df or writes Java object strings

repro: python -c "import pandas as pd; pd.options.future.infer_string=True; from pyspark.sql import SparkSession, functions as F; from rand_engine.main.spark_generator import SparkGenerator; s=SparkSession.builder.master('local[1]').getOrCreate(); s.conf.set('spark.sql.execution.arrow.pyspark.enabled','false'); print(sorted({r.c for r in SparkGenerator(s, F, {'c': {'method': 'distincts', 'kwargs': {'distincts': ['x', 'y', None]}}}).size(200).get_df().collect()}, key=str))"
symptom: With pandas 3 string inference and spark.sql.execution.arrow.pyspark.enabled false (Spark's default), SparkGenerator(spark, F, {'c': {'method': 'distincts', 'kwargs': {'distincts': ['x', 'y', None]}}}).size(200).get_df() yields a string column holding 'x', 'y' and the string 'NaN' instead of null: pd.DataFrame(values) types the column with the string dtype, whose missing value is NaN, and createDataFrame writes it as text. With Arrow on the value is null; on pandas 2 the column is object and keeps None.
title: SparkGenerator writes the string 'NaN' for a None in a text pool on pandas 3
